title: Knowing Is Not Enough: Information Retrievability as a Precondition to Effective LLM Oversight
abstract: arXiv:2609.01976v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in organizational work, yet their errors often pass human review. Prior research locates such failures in users' capability to review LLM output or their engagement in doing so. We develop an alternative, retrieval-based account of human oversight and posit that error detection is more effective when oversight-relevant information is accessible to users at the moment of review. Across two randomized lab-in-the-field experiments with 640 customer-facing employees, we show that self-generated explanations improve error detection and strengthen recall of verification-relevant reasoning, while cues that reactivate such reasoning help sustain detection under repeated LLM use. Theoretically, we identify information retrievability as a distinct precondition for effective oversight and specify generative encoding and cue-supported reactivation as mechanisms that build and sustain it. translated_title: 知晓并不足够：信息可检索性作为有效大语言模型监督的前提条件
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型日益深入地嵌入组织工作之中，然而其错误往往能通过人类审查。先前的研究将这类失败归因于用户审查LLM输出的能力或其参与审查的投入程度。我们提出了一种替代性的、基于检索机制的人类监督解释框架，并主张当与监督相关的信息在审查时刻能够被用户获取时，错误检测会更加有效。通过两项针对640名面向客户员工的随机化现场实验室实验，我们发现自我生成的解释能够改善错误检测并强化对验证相关推理的记忆，而重新激活此类推理的线索有助于在反复使用LLM的过程中维持检测效果。在理论层面，我们识别出信息可检索性是有效监督的一个独特前提条件，并阐明生成性编码与线索支持的重激活是建立和维持这一前提的机制。
tldr: 该研究提出“信息可检索性”是有效监督大语言模型的独特前提条件，并通过640名员工的实验证明，自我生成的解释能强化对验证相关推理的记忆、提升错误检测能力，而线索支持的重激活机制则能在反复使用LLM的过程中持续维持监督效果。
